# Removed surfaces and replacements
Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces

What the July 2026 sweep removed, plus the per-API replacement mappings for removed surfaces and later-window deprecations. Part of the [Plugin SDK migration](/plugins/sdk-migration) guide.

## Removed compatibility surfaces

The July 2026 sweep removed the root SDK and compat barrels, the extension API
bridge, the expired SDK subpath aliases, unused SDK subpaths, and typed-public
access to bundled-only SDK modules. Private-local build mappings remain for
repository owners, and production-private JavaScript exports support official
plugin runtimes. Neither provides typed third-party SDK access.

### Channel, config, and infrastructure compatibility facades

`channel-lifecycle`, `channel-message`, `channel-reply-pipeline`,
`config-runtime`, and `infra-runtime` were removed with SDK-owner approval on
September 30, 2026. Channel imports move to focused outbound and inbound
contracts; config access uses supplied config, snapshots, and mutation helpers;
infrastructure imports move to the matching focused runtime or injected API.
System-event snapshot inspection and consumption use `system-event-runtime`.

Some legacy helpers and named types require caller changes rather than an
import-path substitution. See the [channel mappings](/plugins/sdk-migration/import-paths#retained-channel-facade-mappings)
and [config and infrastructure migration steps](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate).

### Command, Discord, and Telegram account facades

`command-auth`, `discord`, and `telegram-account` were removed with explicit
SDK-owner approval on October 2, 2026. Move sender authorization to
`channel-ingress-runtime`, native command helpers to `command-auth-native`, and
help builders to `command-status`. Discord and Telegram behavior remains owned
by their plugins; use generic channel contracts and injected runtime helpers
from external plugins, and the owning plugin's `api.ts` / `runtime-api.ts`
barrels for repository consumers.

These are breaking removals for third-party plugins that still import the old
subpaths, including older published `@openclaw/discord` packages. Upgrade affected
plugins before upgrading the host. Not every export has a path-only replacement;
see the [per-surface mappings](/plugins/sdk-migration/import-paths#removed-command-and-channel-facades).

### Retroactively recorded shipped exports

The following exports shipped in `v2026.9.8` and were removed without a
compatibility window. Their removals were recorded retroactively on October 7,
2026 when the shipped-surface guard was introduced; the exports remain removed.
The registry's `removeAfter` is the UTC day before the removing commit landed,
not a compatibility window that was offered to plugin authors.

| Removed export (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/` prefix)                 | Landed (UTC) | `removeAfter` | Replacement                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allow-from.mapBasicAllowlistResolutionEntries`                | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; project `BasicAllowlistResolutionEntry` fields in the consuming plugin.                         |
| `computer-use.compileComputerUseValidator`                     | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | `Compile(schema).Check` from `typebox/compile`, using the exported Computer Use schemas.              |
| `extension-shared.runStoppablePassiveMonitor`                  | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | `channel-outbound.runPassiveAccountLifecycle` with `stop: (monitor) => monitor.stop()`.               |
| `gateway-runtime.resolveAdvertisedLanHost`                     | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; advertised LAN host discovery is host-owned.                                                    |
| `json-store.readJsonFileWithFallback`                          | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; own JSON artifact parsing, fallback, and file-existence handling in the plugin.                 |
| `provider-auth.normalizeSecretInputModeInput`                  | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; validate plugin-owned input as the exported `SecretInputMode` values `plaintext` or `ref`.      |
| `persistent-dedupe.PersistentDedupeLegacyJsonMigrationOptions` | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; the legacy JSON migration was retired.                                                          |
| `persistent-dedupe.PersistentDedupeLegacyJsonMigrationResult`  | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; the legacy JSON migration was retired.                                                          |
| `persistent-dedupe.listPersistentDedupeLegacyJsonFileEntries`  | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; the legacy JSON migration was retired.                                                          |
| `persistent-dedupe.migratePersistentDedupeLegacyJsonFile`      | 2026-10-05   | 2026-10-04    | None; the legacy JSON migration was retired. Runtime dedupe continues through the SQLite-backed APIs. |
| `provider-auth.CachedCopilotToken`                             | 2026-10-02   | 2026-10-01    | Provider-local GitHub Copilot auth APIs; none in the public SDK.                                      |
| `provider-auth.DEFAULT_COPILOT_API_BASE_URL`                   | 2026-10-02   | 2026-10-01    | Provider-local GitHub Copilot auth APIs; none in the public SDK.                                      |
| `provider-auth.deriveCopilotApiBaseUrlFromToken`               | 2026-10-02   | 2026-10-01    | Provider-local GitHub Copilot auth APIs; none in the public SDK.                                      |
| `provider-auth.resolveCopilotApiToken`                         | 2026-10-02   | 2026-10-01    | Provider-local GitHub Copilot auth APIs; none in the public SDK.                                      |

The first six exports were removed in
[`2fec39f57319be5b6e0b20b5305665ed1ff5e685`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2fec39f57319be5b6e0b20b5305665ed1ff5e685).
The four legacy JSON migration exports were removed in
[`bd64d93ff1ae704d13813f6580c4809ba0e76606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bd64d93ff1ae704d13813f6580c4809ba0e76606).
The four Copilot exports and their earlier deprecation entries were removed in
[`f2de06b38de710854aacd19218327358445816c8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f2de06b38de710854aacd19218327358445816c8);
third-party plugins must own their provider-specific token exchange and caching.

### Reply silence parsing

`isSilentReplyText` and `isSilentReplyPayloadText` were removed from
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-chunking`. The exact whole-reply classifier remains
available from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime` for raw producer input.
Delivery plugins must forward prepared text without reclassifying it: literal
`NO_REPLY` can be a visible answer.

`SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` was also removed from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-chunking`.
Import it from its existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime` export instead:

```ts

```

Harness producers use `prepareAgentRunTerminalReply` from
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` once on the raw final text, then
render the returned text and publish the matching terminal fact. Deliver the full
returned text rather than the bounded `terminalReply.text` snapshot. An exact uppercase
`NO_REPLY`, ignoring surrounding whitespace, requests silence; punctuation,
quotes, JSON, and prose do not. A literal leading `NO_REPLY\n` removes one line
without reclassifying the suffix. See [Silent replies](/concepts/messages#silent-replies).

### Tool argument redaction

`sanitizeToolArgs` was removed from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`
on October 11, 2026, as part of the maintainer-approved removal of automatic
tool argument and result masking. Remove its import and pass arguments unchanged.
There is no replacement or compatibility masking path. Logging and diagnostic
redaction helpers remain available.

### Process-global API-provider publication

`registerApiProvider(...)` and `unregisterApiProviders(...)` were removed from
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/llm`. They published API transports into process-global
state, which lifecycle-owned model runtimes then had to copy into each prepared
registry.

Provider plugins should register text-inference providers through
`api.registerProvider(...)`. Host-owned code and tests that construct an
`ApiRegistry` should register directly on that registry so provider ownership
and teardown stay scoped to the prepared runtime.

### Deactivate hook alias

The `api.on("deactivate", handler)` compatibility alias was removed. Register
the same shutdown cleanup with `gateway_stop`:

```typescript
// Before
api.on("deactivate", async (event, ctx) => {
  await stopPluginService(ctx);
});

// After
api.on("gateway_stop", async (event, ctx) => {
  await stopPluginService(ctx);
});
```

### Skill Workshop proposal hooks

The `skill_proposal_evaluate` and `skill_proposal_changed` hooks were removed
together with Skill Workshop proposals. Workshop now applies each change
immediately and keeps a restorable version, so there is no pending draft to
evaluate and no proposal lifecycle to observe. The hook runner methods
`runSkillProposalEvaluate` and `runSkillProposalChanged` were removed, and
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry` no longer exports
`PluginHookSkillProposalEvaluateEvent`, `PluginHookSkillProposalEvaluateResult`,
`PluginHookSkillProposalEvaluationOutcome`, `PluginHookSkillProposalChangedEvent`,
`PluginHookSkillProposalKind`, `PluginHookSkillEvaluationFinding`,
`PluginHookSkillBundleFile`, or `PluginHookSkillBundleSnapshot`. The optional
`proposal` field on `PluginHookSkillChangedEvent` was removed too.

To observe committed Workshop skill writes, register `skill_changed` and filter
on `source: "workshop"`. There is no replacement for pre-apply evaluation.
Registering a removed hook name logs an `unknown typed hook` warning and the
handler never runs.

### Private testing barrel

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/testing` was repo-local and excluded from shipped package
artifacts, so it was removed before its 2026-07-28 `removeAfter` date. Repository
tests use focused subpaths such as `plugin-sdk/plugin-test-runtime`,
`plugin-sdk/channel-test-helpers`, `plugin-sdk/channel-target-testing`,
`plugin-sdk/test-env`, and `plugin-sdk/test-fixtures`.

### Credential prompt builder

`buildCredentialSafetyPrompt` remains available from
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. With an options object whose
`controlToolsAvailable` is set from the callable `openclaw` and `gateway` tools, it
returns guidance to use or store user-shared credentials as asked, complete the
task, and briefly acknowledge their use or storage in the final reply without
repeating their values. The acknowledgment stays factual and non-alarming. It also
returns the private login-code handoff guidance and the terminal setup route when
neither control tool is available.

The legacy string argument is deprecated from 2026-09-09 and remains supported
through 2026-11-30. It is accepted and ignored: availability is unknown, so the
helper returns only the private handoff line. Replace strings with
`{ controlToolsAvailable }`; the string form is eligible for removal starting
2026-12-01. The helper itself is not deprecated.

## Migration reference

These mappings cover both removed July 2026 surfaces and later-window active
deprecations. A mapping is migration guidance, not evidence that the old
surface remains available; consult the compatibility registry and removal
timeline for current status.

AccordionGroup

  
Accordion
 command-status">
    **Old (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-auth`)**: `buildCommandsMessage`,
    `buildCommandsMessagePaginated`, `buildHelpMessage`.

    **New (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status`)**: same signatures, imported
    from the narrower subpath. The `command-auth` compatibility re-exports
    have been removed.

    ```typescript
    // Before
    import { buildHelpMessage } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-auth";

    // After
    import { buildHelpMessage } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status";
    ```

  

  
Accordion
 resolveInboundMentionDecision">
    **Old**: `resolveMentionGating(params)` and
    `resolveMentionGatingWithBypass(params)` from
    `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-inbound` or
    `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-mention-gating`.

    **New**: `resolveInboundMentionDecision({ facts, policy })` - one decision
    object instead of two split call shapes.

    Adopted across Discord, iMessage, Matrix, MS Teams, QQBot, Signal,
    Telegram, WhatsApp, and Zalo. Slack's own `app_mention` event model does
    not use this helper.

  

  
Channel runtime shim and channel actions helpers

    `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-runtime` has been removed. Use
    `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-runtime-context` for registering runtime
    objects.

    The native message schema helpers in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-actions`
    were removed alongside raw "actions" channel exports. Expose capabilities
    through the semantic `presentation` surface instead - channel plugins
    declare what they render (cards, buttons, selects) rather than which raw
    action names they accept.

  

  
Accordion
 createTool() on the plugin">
    **Old**: `tool()` factory from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-web-search`.

    **New**: implement `createTool(...)` directly on the provider plugin.
    OpenClaw no longer needs the SDK helper to register the tool wrapper.

  

  
Accordion
 BodyForAgent">
    **Old**: `api.runtime.channel.reply.formatInboundEnvelope(...)` (and the
    `channelEnvelope` field on inbound message objects) to build a flat
    plaintext prompt envelope from inbound channel messages.

    **New**: `BodyForAgent` plus structured user-context blocks. Channel
    plugins attach routing metadata (thread, topic, reply-to, reactions) as
    typed fields instead of concatenating them into a prompt string. The
    `formatAgentEnvelope(...)` helper is still supported for synthesized
    assistant-facing envelopes, but inbound plaintext envelopes are on the way
    out.

    Affected areas: `inbound_claim`, `message_received`, and any custom
    channel plugin that post-processed the old envelope text.

  

  
Accordion
 core thread binding">
    **Old**: `api.on("subagent_spawning", handler)` returning
    `threadBindingReady` or `deliveryOrigin`.

    **New**: let core prepare `thread: true` subagent bindings through the
    channel session-binding adapter. Use `api.on("subagent_spawned", handler)`
    only for post-launch observation.

    ```typescript
    // Before
    api.on("subagent_spawning", async () => ({
      status: "ok",
      threadBindingReady: true,
      deliveryOrigin: { channel: "discord", to: "channel:123", threadId: "456" },
    }));

    // After
    api.on("subagent_spawned", async (event) => {
      await observeSubagentLaunch(event);
    });
    ```

    The `subagent_spawning` hook and its event/result types were removed in
    August 2026 after thread binding moved to the core session-binding path.

  

  
Accordion
 provider catalog types">
    Four discovery type aliases are now thin wrappers over the catalog-era
    types:

    | Old alias                 | New type                  |
    | ------------------------- | ------------------------- |
    | `ProviderDiscoveryOrder`  | `ProviderCatalogOrder`    |
    | `ProviderDiscoveryContext`| `ProviderCatalogContext`  |
    | `ProviderDiscoveryResult` | `ProviderCatalogResult`   |
    | `ProviderPluginDiscovery` | `ProviderPluginCatalog`   |

    The aliases and legacy `ProviderCapabilities` static bag have been
    removed. Provider plugins
    should use explicit provider hooks such as `buildReplayPolicy`,
    `normalizeToolSchemas`, and `wrapStreamFn` rather than a static object.

  

  
Accordion
 resolveThinkingProfile">
    **Old** (three separate hooks on `ProviderThinkingPolicy`):
    `isBinaryThinking(ctx)`, `supportsXHighThinking(ctx)`, and
    `resolveDefaultThinkingLevel(ctx)`.

    **New**: a single `resolveThinkingProfile(ctx)` that returns a
    `ProviderThinkingProfile` with the standard `id`, optional `label`, and a
    ranked level list. OpenClaw clamps unsupported requests by profile rank
    during execution, preserving the stored preference across model switches.

    The context includes `provider`, `modelId`, optional merged `reasoning`,
    and optional merged model `compat` facts. Provider plugins can use those
    catalog facts to expose a model-specific profile only when the configured
    request contract supports it.

    Implement one hook instead of three. The legacy hooks have been removed.

  

  
Accordion
 contracts.externalAuthProviders">
    **Old**: implementing external auth hooks without declaring the provider
    in the plugin manifest.

    **New**: declare `contracts.externalAuthProviders` in the plugin manifest
    **and** implement `resolveExternalAuthProfiles(...)`.

    ```json
    {
      "contracts": {
        "externalAuthProviders": ["anthropic", "openai"]
      }
    }
    ```

  

  
Accordion
 setup.providers[].envVars">
    **Old** manifest field: `providerAuthEnvVars: { anthropic: ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] }`.

    **New**: mirror the same env-var lookup into `setup.providers[].envVars`
    on the manifest. This consolidates setup/status env metadata in one place
    and avoids booting the plugin runtime just to answer env-var lookups.

    `providerAuthEnvVars` is no longer accepted.

  

  
Accordion
 registerMemoryCapability">
    **Old**: three separate calls - `api.registerMemoryPromptSection(...)`,
    `api.registerMemoryFlushPlan(...)`, `api.registerMemoryRuntime(...)`.

    **New**: one call on the memory-state API -
    `registerMemoryCapability(pluginId, { promptBuilder, flushPlanResolver, runtime })`.

    Same slots, single registration call. Additive prompt and corpus helpers
    (`registerMemoryPromptSupplement`, `registerMemoryCorpusSupplement`) are
    not affected.

  

  
Memory embedding provider API

    **Old**: `api.registerMemoryEmbeddingProvider(...)` plus
    `contracts.memoryEmbeddingProviders`.

    **New**: `api.registerEmbeddingProvider(...)` plus
    `contracts.embeddingProviders`.

    The generic embedding provider contract is reusable outside memory and is
    the supported path for every provider. The memory-specific registration API
    and manifest contract were removed after the **2026-08-21** migration
    deadline.

  

  
Accordion
 OutboundDeliveryResult">
    **Old**: return `{ ok, messageId, error }` through
    `ChannelSendRawResult` and normalize it with
    `createRawChannelSendResultAdapter(...)`.

    **New**: return `OutboundDeliveryResult` fields and attach the channel with
    `createAttachedChannelResultAdapter(...)`. Failed sends should throw instead
    of returning an error string. Put the platform destination in
    `target: { kind: "chat" | "channel" | "room" | "conversation", id }`;
    the old parallel `chatId`, `channelId`, `roomId`, and `conversationId`
    result fields are no longer accepted. The raw result type remains available
    until its separately announced ordinary stable removal release.

  

  
Subagent session messages types renamed

    Two legacy type aliases still exported from `src/plugins/runtime/types.ts`:

    | Old                           | New                             |
    | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
    | `SubagentReadSessionParams`   | `SubagentGetSessionMessagesParams` |
    | `SubagentReadSessionResult`   | `SubagentGetSessionMessagesResult` |

    The runtime method `readSession` is deprecated in favor of
    `getSessionMessages`. Same signature; the old method calls through to the
    new one.

  

  
Removed session and transcript file APIs

    The SQLite session/transcript flip removes or deprecates plugin-facing APIs
    that exposed active `sessions.json` stores, JSONL transcript paths, or lists
    of session files. Runtime plugins should use session identity and SDK runtime
    helpers instead of resolving or mutating active files.

    | Migrating surface | Replacement |
    | ----------------- | ----------- |
    | Removed `loadSessionStore(...)` and `resolveSessionStoreEntry(...)`, including package-root `loadSessionStore(...)` | `await getSessionEntryAsync(...)` for one scoped row or `await listSessionEntriesAsync(...)` for scoped metadata iteration from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime`. |
    | Removed `updateSessionStore(...)`, package-root `saveSessionStore(...)`, and SDK file-store writes | `patchSessionEntry(...)`, `upsertSessionEntry(...)`, and `deleteSessionEntry(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime`; mutate only the intended rows instead of replacing a detached whole-store snapshot. |
    | Removed `LoadSessionStoreOptions` and `UpdateSessionStoreOptions` | Parameters accepted by the scoped row APIs; the whole-store cache and callback options no longer apply. |
    | Removed `resolveSessionFilePath(...)` | Session identity (`agentId`, `sessionKey`, and `sessionId`) with `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime`, or Gateway methods that operate on the current session. |
    | Removed `resolveSessionTranscriptPathInDir(...)` and `resolveAndPersistSessionFile(...)` | Session identity and Gateway methods that operate on the current session. |
    | `readLatestAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript(...)` | Identity-backed transcript readers exposed by the current runtime context, or Gateway history/session methods when the plugin is outside the transcript owner path. |
    | `SessionTranscriptUpdate.sessionFile` | `SessionTranscriptUpdate.target` with `agentId`, `sessionKey`, and `sessionId`. |
    | Memory sync inputs such as `sessionFiles` | Identity-backed transcript/session sources provided by the host; do not crawl active JSONL files for live sessions. |
    | Runtime options named `transcriptPath` or `sessionFile` for active sessions | `sessionTarget`/runtime target objects that carry storage-neutral session identity. |

    Legacy JSONL transcript files remain valid as import, archive, export, and
    support artifacts. They are no longer the steady-state runtime contract for
    active sessions.

    The official `@openclaw/codex` and `@openclaw/feishu` plugins released with
    `v2026.7.1-beta.5` imported the retired bridge. SDK-owner approval on
    September 30, 2026 closed its compatibility window early, replacing the
    former October 12 deadline. The supported-plugin cutoff excludes that
    release and any other package still importing the
    bridge. Upgrade affected plugins to versions using the replacements before
    upgrading OpenClaw. A newer version number alone is not evidence of migration.

    `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime` and `resolveStorePath(...)`
    remain supported. Pass the selected `agentId` explicitly to scoped row
    operations; resolving a path no longer records an agent selection for a
    later whole-store call. This removal does not change SQLite schemas or
    legacy-state import and Doctor migrations.

    `openclaw plugins inspect --all --runtime` reports non-bundled plugins whose
    load errors or diagnostics still reference these removed file APIs. The
    `@openclaw/plugin-inspector` advisory sweep must use version `0.3.17` or
    newer so external package scans also flag whole-store session helpers,
    session file-path helpers, legacy transcript file targets, and low-level
    transcript helpers before release.

  

  
Accordion
 V2 host-capability contract">
    New or updated harness plugins should implement `AgentHarnessV2` and use
    `AgentHarnessAttemptParamsV2`, `EmbeddedRunAttemptParamsV2`, or
    `AgentHarnessSideQuestionParamsV2`. The V2 parameter types require
    `hostCapabilities`, matching what core supplies at the selected-harness
    boundary. A plugin that adopts these V2 contracts must declare
    `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: ">=2026.8.1"` (or a newer floor) in its package
    manifest so an older host rejects the plugin before loading it.

    Existing plugins may continue implementing `AgentHarness` and constructing
    the legacy `AgentHarnessAttemptParams`, `EmbeddedRunAttemptParams`, or
    `AgentHarnessSideQuestionParams` types without that field through
    2026-10-12. Those contracts keep the capability optional only for source
    compatibility; they do not create a capability-free runtime path. Migrate
    by changing the imported type name and binding tool or native-action surfaces through
    `params.hostCapabilities`.

  

  
Tasks and TaskFlow APIs removed

    The Tasks registry and TaskFlow orchestration APIs have been removed,
    including `api.runtime.tasks`, `registerDetachedTaskRuntime`, and the
    `agent-harness-task-runtime` SDK subpath. No compatibility facade remains.
    Use native subagent launch/wait/history APIs, cron run history, and the
    ordinary Lobster runner for their respective operations. Harness completion
    routing uses the completion-only `agent-harness-completion` subpath.
    This removal does not change the physical database schemas. Existing
    `task_runs`, `task_delivery_state`, and `flow_runs` tables, columns, and indexes
    remain unchanged. Cron reads and writes only its `runtime = 'cron'` history
    rows in `task_runs`; non-Cron Task and TaskFlow rows remain untouched and
    unused by the runtime. The Codex plugin's
    [Doctor migration](/gateway/doctor/config-migrations#native-codex-recovery-after-tasks-removal)
    preserves eligible owner-stamped native recovery facts in existing parent
    binding metadata, leaving source rows byte-identical. It adds no runtime Task
    reader or replacement SDK surface; current requester authority still governs
    completion delivery. See the [versioning contract](/reference/database-schemas/versioning).
  

  
Accordion
 agent tool-result middleware">
    Covered in [How to migrate](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#how-to-migrate). Included here for
    completeness: the removed embedded-runner-only
    `api.registerEmbeddedExtensionFactory(...)` path is replaced by
    `api.registerAgentToolResultMiddleware(...)` with an explicit runtime list
    in `contracts.agentToolResultMiddleware`.
  

  
Accordion
 OpenClawConfig">
    The `OpenClawSchemaType` root-SDK alias was removed. Use the primary
    `OpenClawConfig` name.

    ```typescript
    // Before
    import type { OpenClawSchemaType } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk";
    // After
    import type { OpenClawConfig } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/config-contracts";
    ```

  

Note

Extension-level deprecations (inside bundled channel/provider plugins under
`extensions/`) are tracked inside their own `api.ts` and `runtime-api.ts`
barrels. They do not affect third-party plugin contracts and are not listed
here. If you consume a bundled plugin's local barrel directly, read the
deprecation comments in that barrel before upgrading.

---

# Migrate synchronous SQLite APIs
Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/sqlite-async

Migrate synchronous SQLite SDK calls to the awaited or prepared replacements
below. **The final compatibility day is December 31, 2026 (`2026-12-31`).**
Removal ships in the **first January 2027 stable release**, without a Plugin SDK
major version. This deprecation release retains the listed contracts; it does
not remove them. See the [removal timeline](/plugins/sdk-migration/removal-timeline)
for the release and shipped-surface gates.

Start with the families your plugin uses. For direct `Async` replacements, keep
the arguments and await the result. Factories that return adapters or prepared
readers may remain synchronous: await the operations on the returned object as
described below. A Promise-returning wrapper around a native database callback
still runs that callback on the caller's thread; migrate the callback contract,
not just its call site.

These changes preserve stored data, schemas, retention, and update behavior.
Await a write before reading its result or publishing an external effect. Never
retry a failed awaited operation through a deprecated synchronous path. Bundled
plugins target the current host and do not need older-host fallbacks. External
plugins should declare the host version that supplies the capabilities they use.

## Session reads and inbound envelopes

Use `session-store-runtime` for session readers and `channel-inbound` for
prepared envelope construction. The same method mapping
applies to `api.runtime.agent.session` and channel runtime aliases.

```ts
// Before
const entry = api.runtime.agent.session.getSessionEntry(target);
// After
const entry = await api.runtime.agent.session.getSessionEntryAsync(target);
```

| Before                                          | After                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getSessionEntry`                               | `await getSessionEntryAsync(...)`                                                                               |
| `getConversationSession`                        | `await getConversationSessionAsync(...)`                                                                        |
| `listSessionEntries`                            | `await listSessionEntriesAsync(...)`                                                                            |
| `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway`            | `await loadCombinedSessionStoreForGatewayAsync(...)` from `session-transcript-hit`                              |
| `readAmbientTranscriptWatermark`                | `await readAmbientTranscriptWatermarkAsync(...)`                                                                |
| `readSessionUpdatedAt`                          | `await readSessionUpdatedAtAsync(...)`                                                                          |
| `resolveTranscriptSessionKeyBySessionId`        | `await resolveTranscriptSessionKeyBySessionIdAsync(...)`                                                        |
| `loadTranscriptEventsSync`                      | `await loadTranscriptEvents(...)`                                                                               |
| `readTranscriptStatsSync`                       | `await readTranscriptStatsAsync(...)`                                                                           |
| `readTranscriptStatsBatchReadOnlySync`          | `await readTranscriptStatsBatchReadOnlyAsync(...)`                                                              |
| `statSessionEntrySync`                          | `await statSessionEntry(...)`                                                                                   |
| `readAcpSessionEntry`                           | `await readAcpSessionEntryAsync(...)`                                                                           |
| `AcpSessionManager.resolveSession`              | `await manager.resolveSessionAsync(...)`                                                                        |
| `createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilder`           | `await createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync(...)`                                                           |
| `resolveChannelInboundRouteEnvelope`            | `resolveAgentRoute(...)`, then `await createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync({ cfg, route })`                 |
| `resolveInboundSessionEnvelopeContext`          | `await resolveInboundSessionEnvelopeContextAsync(...)`                                                          |
| `createInboundEnvelopeBuilder`                  | `await createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync({ cfg, route })`                                                |
| `resolveInboundRouteEnvelopeBuilder`            | `resolveAgentRoute(...)`, then `await createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync({ cfg, route })`                 |
| `resolveInboundRouteEnvelopeBuilderWithRuntime` | Runtime `routing.resolveAgentRoute(...)`, then `await createChannelInboundEnvelopeBuilderAsync({ cfg, route })` |
| `dispatchInboundDirectDmWithRuntime`            | `await dispatchInboundDirectDm(...)`                                                                            |

The historical transcript-key resolver includes retained `session_windows`
after a session resets. `getSessionEntryByIdAsync(...).sessionKey` is not a
replacement for historical lookup. See the [exact historical lookup
contract](/plugins/sdk-migration/async-transcript-and-tts#historical-transcript-keys).

Prepare the envelope builder once per inbound message. It returns a synchronous
formatter yielding the body string; the older generic builder returned
`{ storePath, body }`. If the caller still needs a store path, resolve it from
the same configured store and route through `runtime.channel.session.resolveStorePath`.
For custom formatting, await `readSessionUpdatedAtAsync` once and pass that
timestamp into the formatter instead of retaining a database-reading callback.

`listSessionEntriesAsync` returns a read-only metadata projection, not detached
snapshots such as saved skill prompts. It does not take the synchronous listing's
`readOnly`, snapshot-hydration, or source-capture options. Use
`getSessionEntryAsync` for a full public entry. Keep authorization for transcript
or metadata disclosure at the existing effect boundary. Memory statistics and
archive readers remain on their existing documented or local subpaths; this
migration does not make private host facades public.

For entry writes, replace opaque callbacks with owner preparation or an
already-prepared patch:

| Before                                       | After                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `patchSessionEntry({ update, ...target })`   | `await prepareSessionEntryPatch({ prepare, ...target })`, or `await applySessionEntryPatch({ patch, ...target })` |
| `updateSessionStoreEntry`                    | `prepareSessionEntryPatch` / `applySessionEntryPatch`                                                             |
| `updateLastRoute` with `assertCommitAllowed` | `await updateLastRouteWithAuthority(...)`                                                                         |
| `upsertSessionUpstreamLink`                  | `await upsertSessionUpstreamLinkAsync(...)`                                                                       |
| `deleteSessionUpstreamLink`                  | `await deleteSessionUpstreamLinkAsync(...)`                                                                       |
| Initialization owner's `prepare().link(...)` | Await `prepare()`, then `await prepared.linkAsync(...)`                                                           |

```ts
// Before: a callback depends on the stored entry.
await patchSessionEntry({ ...target, update: choosePatch });
// After: preparation happens outside the transaction; the owner detects conflicts.
await prepareSessionEntryPatch({ ...target, prepare: choosePatch });
```

See [entry patch conflicts and authority](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#prepare-session-entry-changes)
when translating transaction-local callback behavior.

## Auth profiles and provider readiness

Use the public `provider-auth` surface for profile stores and writes. Bundled
plugins also use the private `provider-auth-runtime` surface for profile metadata
and `agent-sessions` for `AuthStorage` and `ModelRegistry`.
Existing `agent-runtime` and runtime `modelAuth` aliases follow the same mapping;
prefer the focused public subpath when one exists.

```ts
// Before
const auth = AuthStorage.forAgent(agentDir, config);
auth.set(providerId, credential);
// After
const auth = await AuthStorage.forAgentAsync(agentDir, config);
await auth.setAsync(providerId, credential);
```

| Before                                                   | After                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ensureAuthProfileStore`                                 | `await ensureAuthProfileStoreAsync(...)`                                                                                       |
| `ensureAuthProfileStoreForLocalUpdate`                   | `await ensureAuthProfileStoreForLocalUpdateAsync(...)`                                                                         |
| `upsertAuthProfile`                                      | `await upsertAuthProfileAsync(...)`                                                                                            |
| `upsertApiKeyProfile`                                    | `await upsertApiKeyProfileAsync(...)`                                                                                          |
| `isProviderApiKeyConfigured`                             | `await isProviderApiKeyConfiguredAsync(...)`                                                                                   |
| `isProviderAuthProfileConfigured`                        | `await isProviderAuthProfileConfiguredAsync(...)`                                                                              |
| `listUsableProviderAuthProfileIds`                       | `await listUsableProviderAuthProfileIdsAsync(...)`                                                                             |
| `resolveProviderAuthProfileMetadata`                     | `await resolveProviderAuthProfileMetadataAsync(...)`                                                                           |
| `loadAuthProfileStoreWithoutExternalProfiles`            | `await loadAuthProfileStoreWithoutExternalProfilesAsync(...)`                                                                  |
| `loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntime`                         | `await loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntimeAsync(...)`                                                                               |
| `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime`                  | `await loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntimeAsync(agentDir, { ...options, readOnly: true, allowKeychainPrompt: false })`              |
| `saveAuthProfileStore`                                   | `await updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock(...)` from `provider-auth`; mutate the current store under its owner                     |
| `findPersistedAuthProfileCredential`                     | `await findPersistedAuthProfileCredentialAsync(...)`                                                                           |
| `resolvePersistedAuthProfileOwnerAgentDir`               | `await resolvePersistedAuthProfileOwnerAgentDirAsync(...)`                                                                     |
| `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay`                         | Retire physical database-path displays; display provider/profile identifiers instead. No public async path replacement.        |
| `replaceRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshots`                | `await replaceRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshotsAsync(...)`                                                                      |
| `AuthStorage.create(authPath)`                           | `await AuthStorage.forAgentAsync(agentDir)` using the path's owning agent directory                                            |
| `AuthStorage.forAgent`                                   | `await AuthStorage.forAgentAsync(...)`                                                                                         |
| `AuthStorage.reload`                                     | `await auth.reloadAsync(...)`                                                                                                  |
| `AuthStorage.set`                                        | `await auth.setAsync(...)`                                                                                                     |
| `AuthStorage.remove`                                     | `await auth.removeAsync(...)`                                                                                                  |
| `AuthStorage.logout`                                     | `await auth.logoutAsync(...)`                                                                                                  |
| `ModelRegistry.create`                                   | `await ModelRegistry.createAsync(...)`, or SQL-free `ModelRegistry.fromCapturedSources(...)` when sources are already prepared |
| `ModelRegistry.refresh`                                  | `await registry.refreshAsync(...)`                                                                                             |
| `ModelRegistry.unregisterProvider`                       | `await registry.unregisterProviderAsync(...)`                                                                                  |
| `resolveModelAuthMode`                                   | `await resolveModelAuthModeAsync(...)`                                                                                         |
| `formatModelsAvailableHeader`                            | `await formatModelsAvailableHeaderAsync(...)`                                                                                  |
| `resolveCapabilityModelCandidates`                       | `await resolveCapabilityModelCandidatesAsync(...)`                                                                             |
| `resolveConfiguredCapabilityProvider`                    | `await resolveConfiguredCapabilityProviderAsync(...)`                                                                          |
| `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProvider`                 | `await resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProviderAsync(...)`                                                                       |
| `getTtsProvider`                                         | `await getTtsProviderAsync(...)`                                                                                               |
| `isTtsProviderConfigured`                                | `await isTtsProviderConfiguredAsync(...)`                                                                                      |
| `resolveExplicitTtsOverrides`                            | `await resolveExplicitTtsOverridesAsync(...)`                                                                                  |
| Runtime `webSearch.listProviders`                        | `await webSearch.listProvidersAsync(...)`                                                                                      |
| `api.runtime.agent.resolveCliBackendDispatchEligibility` | `await api.runtime.agent.resolveCliBackendDispatchEligibilityAsync(...)`                                                       |

Harnesses should consume the host-prepared `params.authStorage`. `AuthStorage`
`get`, `list`, and `has` remain synchronous reads of its prepared view; `login`
and `getApiKey` already return promises. Do not replace a newer whole auth store
with a previously loaded snapshot: use `updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock` for
owner-backed mutation.

Physical database-path displays are retired after 2026-12-31. External plugins
should display provider/profile identifiers; there is no public async API for
the selected database path. The private bundled-plugin helper
`AuthStorage.resolvePathForDisplayAsync` preserves agent-local-versus-shared
database selection, including locators for profiles that do not exist yet.
Metadata helpers return profile/account identities and are not path substitutes.

Provider readiness hooks add an awaited callback:

| Before                                                               | After                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `ImageGenerationProvider.isConfigured`                               | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `MusicGenerationProvider.isConfigured`                               | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `VideoGenerationProvider.isConfigured`                               | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `SpeechProviderPlugin.isConfigured`                                  | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `RealtimeTranscriptionProviderPlugin.isConfigured`                   | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin.isConfigured`                           | `isConfiguredAsync`                      |
| `RealtimeVoiceProviderPlugin.resolveConfig`                          | `resolveConfigAsync`                     |
| `InternalRealtimeVoiceProviderApi.isBrowserSessionConfigured`        | `isBrowserSessionConfiguredAsync`        |
| `InternalRealtimeVoiceProviderApi.isGatewayRelayConfigured`          | `isGatewayRelayConfiguredAsync`          |
| `InternalRealtimeVoiceProviderApi.resolveBrowserSessionCapabilities` | `resolveBrowserSessionCapabilitiesAsync` |

```ts
// Before
isConfigured: (context) => isProviderApiKeyConfigured(context),
// After
// Preserve synchronous SDK callers through 2026-12-31.
isConfigured: (context) => isProviderApiKeyConfigured(context),
isConfiguredAsync: async (context) => await isProviderApiKeyConfiguredAsync(context),
```

Use the hook's existing context and provider-specific inputs. The host awaits
readiness and prefers the async hook; a failed async hook is not retried through
the legacy one. A readiness result does not authorize later credential use.
Keep the synchronous hooks required by the provider type through 2026-12-31.
Bundled providers also retain synchronous hooks to support callers of the public
synchronous SDK APIs until that date; ordinary runtime callers use async hooks.
See [auth and availability details](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#await-auth-profile-and-provider-availability-operations).

## Approval routing and command authorization

Direct resolvers return promises. Factories whose names end in `Async` below
still return adapters synchronously; their routing and eligibility callbacks
return promises and the host awaits them.

```ts
// Before
const auth = resolveCommandAuthorization(input);
// After
const auth = await resolveCommandAuthorizationAsync(input);

// Factory migration: construction itself stays synchronous.
const adapter = createChannelApprovalNativeRuntimeAdapterAsync(options);
```

## Conversation and native session bindings

Create current-host managers with `createAccountScopedConversationBindingManagerV2`
and register custom adapters with `registerSessionBindingAdapterV2`. The V2
manager factory remains synchronous and returns an async-only receiver.

```ts
// Before
const manager = createAccountScopedConversationBindingManager(options);
const binding = manager.getByConversationId(conversationId);
// After
const manager = createAccountScopedConversationBindingManagerV2(options);
const binding = await manager.getByConversationIdAsync(conversationId);
```

| Before                                                                                                                 | After                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Service or adapter `resolveByConversation`                                                                             | `resolveByConversationAsync`                                                        |
| Service or adapter `listBySession`                                                                                     | `listBySessionAsync`                                                                |
| Adapter `inspectByConversation`                                                                                        | `inspectByConversationAsync`                                                        |
| `inspectSessionBindingByConversation`                                                                                  | `await inspectSessionBindingByConversationAsync(...)`                               |

| `setMatrixThreadBindingMaxAgeBySessionKey`                                                                             | `await setMatrixThreadBindingMaxAgeBySessionKeyAsync(...)`                          |

Channel-specific setter names remain on their existing local channel surfaces.
They do not create new cross-plugin imports. Custom adapters own their storage
and must implement the V2 asynchronous and current-owner contracts.

Native harnesses must migrate ownership, not just rename a getter:

| Before                                        | After                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `captureNativeSessionGenerationAuthority`     | Await `prepareNativeSessionGenerationAuthority`, or use the current retained preparation API below |
| `resolveNativeSessionBinding`                 | Await `resolvePreparedNativeSessionBinding` and release its capture                                |
| `reclaimNativeSessionGeneration`              | Prepare authority, then `await reclaimNativeSessionGenerationWithAuthority(...)`                   |
| `NativeSessionGenerationOperations`           | `NativeSessionGenerationOperationsV2`                                                              |
| `createNativeSessionBindingLifecycle`         | `createNativeSessionBindingLifecycleV2`                                                            |
| `NativeSessionBindingStateStore`              | `NativeSessionBindingStateStoreV2`                                                                 |
| `resolveNativeSessionBindingWithAuthority`    | Await `resolvePreparedNativeSessionBinding` and release its capture                                |
| `AgentHarness.resolveSessionRuntimeOwnership` | `resolveSessionRuntimeOwnershipAsync`                                                              |

For new harness code, follow [native session lineage](/plugins/sdk-migration#native-session-lineage):
await `resolvePreparedNativeSessionBinding` or
`retainNativeSessionGenerationAuthority`, consume the owned capture, and call
`release()` in `finally`. Keep the owner alive through effects and terminal
cleanup. A cold or invalidated cached binding cannot substitute for current
owner authority.

## Keyed state

Use `api.runtime.state.openKeyedStoreV2`, or the lazy
`createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2` factory from `plugin-state-store-runtime` when
providing an explicit plugin owner. These factories return immediately; their
methods perform the worker operations.

```ts
// Before
const store = api.runtime.state.openSyncKeyedStore(options);
store.register("item", value);
const stored = store.lookup("item");
// After
const store = api.runtime.state.openKeyedStoreV2(options);
await store.register("item", value);
const stored = await store.lookup("item");
```

| Before                                                                            | After                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openSyncKeyedStore`, `createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore`                           | `openKeyedStoreV2`, `createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2`                                       |
| Sync `register`, `registerIfAbsent`                                               | Await V2 `register`, `registerIfAbsent`                                                   |
| Sync `lookup`, `lookupMany`                                                       | Await V2 `lookup`, `lookupMany`                                                           |
| Sync `consume`, `delete`                                                          | Await V2 `consume`, `delete`                                                              |
| Sync `entries`, `count`, `clear`                                                  | Await V2 `entries`, `count`, `clear`                                                      |
| Sync `update`, `deleteIf`                                                         | V2 `observe` plus `compareAndApply`, or an owner-defined worker `createOperation`         |
| V1 `openKeyedStore` / `createPluginStateKeyedStore` receiver `update`, `deleteIf` | Open V2 and replace the callback with `observe` / `compareAndApply`, or `createOperation` |

V1 callback methods already return promises, but their opaque JavaScript
callbacks still execute in a native host transaction. Do not replace an atomic
update with an unconditional lookup and write:

```ts
// Before
await legacyStore.update("counter", (value) => (value ?? 0) + 1);
// After
const observed = await store.observe("counter");
const result = await store.compareAndApply("counter", observed.comparison, {
  operation: "update",
  action: "set",
  value: (observed.value ?? 0) + 1,
});
if (result.status === "conflict") {
  // Recompute from a new observation or report the conflict to the caller.
}
```

For `deleteIf`, evaluate the predicate from an observation, then conditionally
apply `{ operation: "delete", action: "delete" }` with that observation's
comparison. A conflict means no requested mutation committed. Do not replay an
unknown write or a callback with external side effects. See [keyed-state
migration](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#await-plugin-state-and-conversation-bindings)
for multi-key conditions and worker operations. Ordinary V1 data-only methods
are not the callback removal target.

// After

## Transcript write callbacks, readers, and catalogs

| Before                                                                                                                                                    | After                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `withSessionTranscriptWriteLock`                                                                                                                          | `await withSessionTranscriptWrite(...)`                                                           |
| `withCodexSessionTranscriptMirrorWriteLock`                                                                                                               | `await withCodexSessionTranscriptMirrorWrite(...)`                                                |
| Lock append or `appendSessionTranscriptMessageByIdentity` / `appendSessionTranscriptMessageByIdentityStrict` option `prepareMessageAfterIdempotencyCheck` | `preparation.prepareMessage`, which may return a promise                                          |
| Those appends' `beforeFreshMessageCommit` option                                                                                                          | `preparation.source` using the host-owned source assertion                                        |
| `loadArchivedSessions`                                                                                                                                    | `await loadArchivedSessionsAsync(...)`                                                            |
| `resolveMemorySessionTargets`                                                                                                                             | `await resolveMemorySessionTargetsAsync(...)`                                                     |
| `loadMemorySessionMetadata`                                                                                                                               | `await loadMemorySessionMetadataAsync(...)`, or `loadMemorySessionMetadataBatchAsync` for a batch |
| `readSessionTranscriptCatalogTitle`                                                                                                                       | `await readSessionTranscriptCatalogTitleAsync(...)`                                               |
| `createSessionCatalogSourceActorProjector`                                                                                                                | `await prepareSessionCatalogSourceActorProjector(...)`                                            |
| `createSessionCatalogGitHubLinker`                                                                                                                        | `await prepareSessionCatalogGitHubLinker(...)`                                                    |
| `validateCodexSessionTranscriptReadAdmission`                                                                                                             | `await validateCodexSessionTranscriptReadAdmissionAsync(...)`                                     |
| `validateCodexSessionTranscriptContextVersion`                                                                                                            | `await validateCodexSessionTranscriptContextVersionAsync(...)`                                    |

```ts
// Before
await withSessionTranscriptWriteLock(target, async (writer) => {
  await writer.appendMessage({ message, prepareMessageAfterIdempotencyCheck: prepareSync });
});
// After
await withSessionTranscriptWrite(target, async (writer) => {
  await writer.appendMessage({
    message,
    preparation: { prepareMessage: prepareAsync, source: sourceAuthority },
  });
});
```

Preparation runs after duplicate detection and outside the database transaction.
Return `undefined` to suppress a fresh append; a duplicate keeps its stored bytes
and skips preparation. Keep externally visible side effects out of preparation.
The new write scope does not promise the old callback's native transaction view
or roll back already committed appends. See [locked transcript
preparation](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#await-locked-transcript-preparation).

`onPreparedAgentRunStart` must still return completion ownership synchronously;

| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `modelAccountConnectService.listLinks`, `link`, `unlink`, `list`, `select`, `status`, `cancel` | Await `listLinksAsync`, `linkAsync`, `unlinkAsync`, `listAsync`, `selectAsync`, `statusAsync`, `cancelAsync` |

| Personal GitHub `cancelAuthorization`, `disconnect`                                            | Await `cancelAuthorizationAsync`, `disconnectAsync`                                                          |
| `getRuntimeConfig` on `runtime-config-snapshot` / `memory-core-host-runtime-core`              | Prepared `readRuntimeConfig()`; for cold preparation, `await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()()`            |
| `resolveCronStorePath`                                                                         | `await resolveCronStorePathAsync(...)`                                                                       |
| `OpenClawPluginNodeHostCommandContext.acquireManagedWorkspace`                                 | `await context.acquireManagedWorkspaceAsync(...)`; release the lease in `finally`                            |
| `ensureAgentWorkspace.beforePersistentApply`                                                   | Await owner preparation before the call and use the SQL-free `guard.assertHost` at the effect                |
| Unprepared `resolveTtsPrefsPath`                                                               | `await resolveTtsPrefsPathAsync(...)`, or pass `preparedTtsPreferences`                                      |
| Unprepared `buildTtsSystemPromptHint`                                                          | `await api.runtime.tts.buildSystemPromptHintAsync(...)`                                                      |

```ts
// Before
const hint = buildTtsSystemPromptHint(config, agentId);
// After
const prepareHint = api.runtime.tts.buildSystemPromptHintAsync;
if (!prepareHint) {
  throw new Error("Update OpenClaw to use async TTS prompt preparation.");

```

Bundled plugins can call private `prepareTtsPreferences` once per turn and pass
that result to the supported prepared overloads. Those SQL-free synchronous
overloads are not deprecated. External plugins use the public runtime method
above. See the [public TTS preparation
recipe](/plugins/sdk-migration/async-transcript-and-tts#tts-prompts).

## Debug proxy capture and raw SQLite

| Before                                                                                 | After                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DebugProxyCaptureStore`, `getDebugProxyCaptureStore`, `acquireDebugProxyCaptureStore` | `await acquireDebugProxyCaptureStoreAsync(...)`; await methods on `lease.store`                                    |
| `closeDebugProxyCaptureStore`                                                          | `await lease.release()` in `finally`                                                                               |
| `DebugProxyCaptureReader`, `createDebugProxyCaptureReader`                             | `AsyncDebugProxyCaptureReader`, `createDebugProxyCaptureReaderAsync`; factory stays synchronous, reads are awaited |
| `initializeDebugProxyCapture`                                                          | `await initializeDebugProxyCaptureAsync(...)`                                                                      |
| `captureHttpExchange`                                                                  | `await captureHttpExchangeAsync(...)`                                                                              |
| `captureWsEvent`, capture context `captureWsEvent`                                     | `await captureWsEventAsync(...)`                                                                                   |
| `finalizeDebugProxyCapture`                                                            | `await finalizeDebugProxyCaptureAsync(...)`                                                                        |

```ts
// Before
const store = acquireDebugProxyCaptureStore(options);
// After
const lease = await acquireDebugProxyCaptureStoreAsync(options);
try {
  // Await capture operations on lease.store.
} finally {
  await lease.release();
}
```

The following `sqlite-runtime` operations have no mechanical async SQL wrapper.
Use `openOpenClawAgentSqliteWorkerStoreV2` and serializable owner commands for
ordinary runtime storage. Move the native implementation into the paired worker
backend using `sqlite-worker-runtime`:

| Before                                                                                                                                 | After                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Writable `openNodeSqliteDatabase`, `openOpenClawAgentDatabase`, `borrowOpenClawAgentDatabase`                                          | Worker store acquisition, preparation, and data-only commands     |
| Legacy worker-store `publicationSource.DatabaseSync`                                                                                   | V2 worker-store publication source                                |
| `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseAsync`, `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseWrite`, `runOpenClawAgentWriteAdmission`                                   | Await V2 worker-store commands; do not pass native host callbacks |
| `runSqliteImmediateTransaction`, `runSqliteImmediateTransactionSync`                                                                   | Transaction inside the worker backend                             |
| `executeSqliteQuerySync`, `executeSqliteQueryTakeFirstSync`, `iterateSqliteQuerySync`, `prepareSqliteQuerySync`, `getNodeSqliteKysely` | Worker-local primitives; expose a data-only operation to the host |

```ts
// Before: awaiting admission does not move this callback off the host.
await withOpenClawAgentDatabaseWrite(options, ({ db }) => updateRows(db, input));
// After: updateRows and its transaction belong to the paired worker backend.
await store.execute({ type: "updateRows", input }, owner.assertCurrent);
```

Preserve explicit read-only inspection, offline Doctor/CLI maintenance custody,
and supported worker-local primitives. Do not treat them as permission for
writable native handles in Gateway handlers. See [worker store construction,
cleanup, and missing-store semantics](/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#replace-native-sqlite-runtime-writes).

## Verify the migration

Exercise one read after an awaited in-process write for each migrated owner.
For conditional state updates, prove that a competing write produces a conflict
instead of being lost. Check callback completion and release resources in
`finally`. Confirm that the migrated flow emits no synchronous SQLite
deprecation warning and that errors propagate without a legacy retry.

This guide covers the synchronous SQLite removal window. Unrelated aliases,
active compatibility records, prepared SQL-free overloads, and private/internal
implementation kernels retain their own contracts. Removing the public adapters
in January does not authorize removing live security checks or changing stored
data.

# Talk and realtime voice migration
Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/talk

The unified Talk session controller, its supported session combinations, and the method map from the removed Talk families. Part of the [Plugin SDK migration](/plugins/sdk-migration) guide.

## Talk and realtime voice migration

Realtime voice, telephony, meeting, and browser Talk code shares one Talk
session controller exported by `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice`. The
controller owns the common Talk event envelope, active turn state, capture
state, output-audio state, recent event history, and stale-turn rejection.
Provider plugins own vendor-specific realtime sessions. Browser-meeting plugins
use `openclaw/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime` for session, browser, audio, node-host,
agent-consult, and voice-call mechanics, then implement `MeetingPlatformAdapter`
for URL rules, DOM scripts, manual-action mapping, captions, creation, and dial-in
plans. Platform REST APIs, OAuth, artifacts, selectors, and wire names remain in
the plugin. Browser permission plans receive the requested meeting URL so each
platform can grant only its exact supported origins. Session runtimes must also
normalize platform-specific live health after confirmed browser departure;
historical transcript fields may remain, but caption and audio readiness must
not stay active after leave.

All bundled surfaces run on the shared controller: browser relay,
managed-room handoff, voice-call realtime, voice-call streaming STT, Google
Meet realtime, and native push-to-talk. Gateway advertises one live Talk event
channel in `hello-ok.features.events`: `talk.event`.

New code should not call `createTalkEventSequencer(...)` directly unless
implementing a low-level adapter or test fixture. Use the shared controller so
turn-scoped events cannot be emitted without a turn id, stale `turnEnd` /
`turnCancel` calls cannot clear a newer active turn, and output-audio
lifecycle events stay consistent across telephony, meetings, browser relay,
managed-room handoff, and native Talk clients.

The public API shape:

```typescript
// Gateway-owned Talk session API.
await gateway.request("talk.session.create", {
  mode: "realtime",
  transport: "gateway-relay",
  brain: "agent-consult",
  sessionKey: "main",
});
await gateway.request("talk.session.appendAudio", { sessionId, audioBase64 });
// Capture this before stopping playback from the active output `talk.event`.
const turnId = activeOutputTalkEvent.talkEvent.turnId;
await gateway.request("talk.session.cancelOutput", { sessionId, turnId, reason: "barge-in" });
await gateway.request("talk.session.submitToolResult", {
  sessionId,
  callId,
  result: { status: "working" },
  options: { willContinue: true },
});
await gateway.request("talk.session.submitToolResult", {
  sessionId,
  callId,
  result: { status: "already_delivered" },
  options: { suppressResponse: true },
});
await gateway.request("talk.session.submitToolResult", { sessionId, callId, result });
await gateway.request("talk.session.close", { sessionId });

// Client-owned provider session API.
await gateway.request("talk.client.create", {
  mode: "realtime",
  transport: "webrtc",
  brain: "agent-consult",
  sessionKey: "main",
});
await gateway.request("talk.client.toolCall", { sessionKey, callId, name, args });
await gateway.request("talk.client.steer", { sessionKey, text, mode: "steer" });
```

Browser-owned WebRTC/provider-websocket sessions use `talk.client.create`,
because the browser owns provider negotiation and media transport while the
Gateway owns credentials, instructions, and tool policy. `talk.session.*` is
the common Gateway-managed surface for gateway-relay realtime, gateway-relay
transcription, and managed-room native STT/TTS sessions.

Legacy configs that place realtime selectors beside `talk.provider` /
`talk.providers` should be repaired with `openclaw doctor --fix`; runtime Talk
does not reinterpret speech/TTS provider config as realtime provider config.

The supported `talk.session.create` combinations are intentionally small:

| Mode            | Transport       | Brain           | Owner              | Notes                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `realtime`      | `gateway-relay` | `agent-consult` | Gateway            | Full-duplex provider audio bridged through the Gateway; tool calls route through the agent-consult tool.           |
| `transcription` | `gateway-relay` | `none`          | Gateway            | Streaming STT only; callers send input audio and receive transcript events.                                        |
| `stt-tts`       | `managed-room`  | `agent-consult` | Native/client room | Push-to-talk and walkie-talkie style rooms where the client owns capture/playback and the Gateway owns turn state. |
| `stt-tts`       | `managed-room`  | `direct-tools`  | Native/client room | Admin-only room mode for trusted first-party surfaces that execute Gateway tool actions directly.                  |

Method map for readers migrating from the older `talk.realtime.*` /
`talk.transcription.*` / `talk.handoff.*` families (all removed):

| Old                              | New                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `talk.realtime.session`          | `talk.client.create`                                 |
| `talk.realtime.toolCall`         | `talk.client.toolCall`                               |
| `talk.realtime.relayAudio`       | `talk.session.appendAudio`                           |
| `talk.realtime.relayCancel`      | `talk.session.cancelOutput`                          |
| `talk.realtime.relayToolResult`  | `talk.session.submitToolResult`                      |
| `talk.realtime.relayStop`        | `talk.session.close`                                 |
| `talk.transcription.session`     | `talk.session.create({ mode: "transcription" })`     |
| `talk.transcription.relayAudio`  | `talk.session.appendAudio`                           |
| `talk.transcription.relayCancel` | `talk.session.close`                                 |
| `talk.transcription.relayStop`   | `talk.session.close`                                 |
| `talk.handoff.create`            | `talk.session.create({ transport: "managed-room" })` |
| `talk.handoff.revoke`            | `talk.session.close`                                 |

The unified control vocabulary is also deliberately narrow:

| Method                          | Applies to                                              | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `talk.session.appendAudio`      | `realtime/gateway-relay`, `transcription/gateway-relay` | Append a base64 PCM audio chunk to the provider session owned by the same Gateway connection.                                                                                                                             |
| `talk.session.cancelOutput`     | `realtime/gateway-relay`                                | Stop assistant audio output without necessarily ending the user turn.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `talk.session.submitToolResult` | `realtime/gateway-relay`                                | Complete a provider tool call after any asynchronous completion exposed by its bridge; pass `options.willContinue` for interim output or, when supported, `options.suppressResponse` to avoid another assistant response. |
| `talk.session.steer`            | agent-backed Talk sessions                              | Send spoken `status`, `steer`, `cancel`, or `followup` control to the active embedded run resolved from the Talk session.                                                                                                 |
| `talk.session.close`            | all unified sessions                                    | Stop relay sessions or revoke managed-room state, then forget the unified session id.                                                                                                                                     |

Do not introduce provider or platform special cases in core to make this work.
Core owns Talk session semantics. Provider plugins own vendor session setup.
Voice-call and Google Meet own telephony/meeting adapters. Browser and native
apps own device capture/playback UX.
